_note: Starter task keys for the sample department. Replace with tasks written for the real department before the pilot, and run validate_against_department first. Briefs are facts, grids and diary notes, never the sentences the participant should produce.

tasks.title: A lecturer's own availability
brief: Shown as a week grid with cells shaded: all of Friday is shaded.
Wednesday periods 4, 5 and 6 are shaded in a lighter tone, with a key reading 'would rather avoid'.
A note on the grid: 'earliest acceptable start: period 2'.
tasks.notes: Shading, not sentences. The hard/soft split is carried by the key ('would rather avoid'), which is the ambiguity Phase 4.3 has to resolve.

tasks.title: Room requirements for a practical
brief: Equipment list for the course: 38 networked workstations.
Room inventory extract: R201 Computer Lab A seats 50; R202 Computer Lab B seats 24; R203 Hardware Lab seats 30.
Department rule card: a course must not be placed in a room smaller than its cohort.
tasks.notes: The facts imply a computer lab and rule out R202 and R203 on capacity, so only R201 fits. A participant naming R201 directly scores as spurious against this key; decide before the pilot whether course_requires_room(CS202L, R201) should also count, and record the decision in the pre-registration.

tasks.title: Two courses and a cohort
brief: Diary note from the Year 2 coordinator: 'CS201 and CS202 both belong to G2A. They ended up in the same slot last semester and the students could not attend both.'
Second note: 'Four periods back to back was too much for them, though we managed.'
tasks.notes: 'could not attend' is a hard cue; 'though we managed' marks the second as soft. Tests whether the cue rules survive reported speech.

tasks.title: A request the schema cannot express
brief: Email extract from Ms. Priya Nair (L005): 'Could you keep my teaching to two days a week?'

intended.note: Caps distinct teaching days per lecturer; no frozen type expresses a count of days.

tasks.notes: A control. The correct outcome is to recognise that nothing in the vocabulary fits. A participant who forces it into lecturer_unavailable scores wrong_type, which is the finding, not a failure.
